 Cricket-South Africa make one change for series decider against Australia
 Monday, 26 Oct 2026
 | 8:03 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Cricket - First Test - South Africa v West Indies - SuperSport Park Cricket Stadium, Centurion, South Africa - March 1, 2023 South Africa's Gerald Coetzee reacts REUTERS/Siphiwe Sibeko/File Photo 
 CAPE TOWN, Oct 26 (Reuters) - South ⁠Africa have made one change to their team for the third ⁠and final test against Australia at Newlands with fast bowler GeraldCoetzee ‌replacing injured Anrich Nortje.
 South Africa have opted to otherwise stick with the players who secured an innings and 31-run victory in the second test in Gqeberha to level the series at 1-1.
 The ​fiery Coetzee earned the last of his four ⁠test caps two years ago.
 “He is ⁠probably the closest guy in terms of like-for-like withNortje as an enforcer in ⁠the ‌bowling attack,” South Africa captain TembaBavuma told reporters on Monday. “Gerald has that extra bit of pace. He has been getting his workloads in ⁠and we think he can make a big play ​for the team.”
 There have ‌been 61 tests at Newlands since 1889, but never one in October, ⁠and only ​three in November, all against Australia.
 The touring side won the first two in 1902 and 1921, but the most recent November fixture was an eight-wicket victory for South Africa ⁠in 2011 when Australia were bowled out for ​47 in their second innings.
 “We have played first-class cricket at this time of year at Newlands, but the way they prepare the wickets for first-class games and ⁠tests is quite different. So there is that element of the experience being new to us,”Bavuma said.
 South Africa can go top of the world rankings with victory, and take a step closer to the World Test Championship final, which they ​won last year against Australia at Lord’s.
 “There is ⁠a lot of cricket to be played before we get closer to the (WTC) final ​against England, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka," Bavuma said. "It ‌is going to be a tough encounter (against ​Australia) and we want to see guys go out and do special things for the team.”
 (Reporting by Nick Said, editing by Ed Osmond)
